binders: An arbitrary type Omega equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure mu on Omega, equipped with the assumption that mu is a probability measure.
Two arbitrary real-valued functions X,Y : Omega -> Real.
hypotheses: The quadratic-exponential infimum scale of X is finite, meaning it is strictly below infinity in ENNReal.
The quadratic-exponential infimum scale of Y is finite.
conclusions: The absolute-exponential infimum scale of the pointwise product omega -> X(omega)Y(omega) is finite.
That product scale is at most the ENNReal product of the quadratic-exponential infimum scale of X and the quadratic-exponential infimum scale of Y.
mathematical_definitions: For a real-valued Z, define A_mu(Z) as the ENNReal infimum of all finite nonzero t such that Z is measurable, exp(|Z|/t.toReal) is mu-integrable, and its integral is at most 2.
For a real-valued Z, define Q_mu(Z) as the ENNReal infimum of all finite nonzero t such that Z is measurable, exp(Z^2/(t.toReal)^2) is mu-integrable, and its integral is at most 2.
Finiteness means strict inequality below the ENNReal top element infinity.
The product X Y is pointwise real multiplication, while Q_mu(X)Q_mu(Y) is multiplication in ENNReal.
translation.proposition_plain_english: On any probability space, if the quadratic-exponential infimum scales Q_mu(X) and Q_mu(Y) of two real-valued functions are both finite, then the absolute-exponential infimum scale A_mu(XY) of their pointwise product is finite and satisfies A_mu(XY) <= Q_mu(X) Q_mu(Y).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: No independence, centering, symmetry, identical-distribution, or other relation between X and Y is assumed.
Measurability is not a separate target hypothesis; it is built into every admissible scale, and finite quadratic-exponential infimum scales rule out the empty-admissible-set top case.
Both input scales are assumed finite, but they may equal zero because zero is excluded only as an admissible candidate, not necessarily as an infimum.
All scales are ENNReal infima over finite nonzero candidates; the theorem does not assert that any infimum is attained.
The threshold in every exponential-moment condition is exactly 2, and the displayed multiplicative bound has no extra constant.
Every candidate scale includes an explicit Integrable condition, so its bound is not based on a totalized integral of a nonintegrable function.
The conclusion concerns only the absolute-exponential scale of the pointwise product; it does not assert a quadratic-exponential bound for that product.
ambiguities: The complete-order infrastructure defines infima even for exceptional admissible sets, but the packet does not narrate the empty-set convention; the finite input hypotheses avoid that case for X and Y.
The Bochner integral is exposed through an opaque wrapper, but behavior outside integrability is immaterial within admissible sets because Integrable is explicitly conjoined.
The descriptive names A_mu and Q_mu are introduced only for this translation; the dossier presents the two infimum constructions anonymously.
